questions.stem: The irrational fear of heights is called:
questions.explanation: Acro- (Greek: 'height, summit') + phobia. Claustrophobia — enclosed spaces. Xenophobia — foreigners / strangers. Hydrophobia — water (also a classic symptom of rabies, which is why the disease itself is sometimes called hydrophobia). Agoraphobia — open / public spaces.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: Arachne (Greek: spider) + phobia. Spielberg's 1990 film 'Arachnophobia' used the word as its title. Fear of snakes = ophidiophobia. Fear of germs = mysophobia (germophobia). Fear of crowds = enochlophobia / demophobia. Fear of public speaking (very high-hit) = glossophobia.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.explanation: Agora (Greek: open marketplace, public gathering place) + phobia. Sufferers feel panic in crowded public places and often in places from which escape may be difficult. Claustrophobia is the opposite — fear of closed / small spaces (elevators, MRIs). Fear of darkness = nyctophobia.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: An obsession or craze for books — especially for collecting them — is called:
questions.explanation: 'Biblio' — book; 'mania' — obsessive desire or madness. Kleptomania — compulsion to steal (even trivial things). Pyromania — compulsion to start fires. Egomania — obsessive self-centredness. Megalomania — grandiose delusions. The '-phile' form gives 'bibliophile' (book-lover, without the pathology).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: The fear of being in enclosed or confined spaces is called:
questions.explanation: Latin 'claustrum' (enclosed space) + Greek 'phobia'. Common triggers — elevators, MRI machines, small rooms, aircraft cabins. Different from agoraphobia (opposite: fear of open / public places). Acrophobia — heights. Xenophobia — strangers / foreigners.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Match the phobia with its trigger. A. Hydrophobia. B. Ophidiophobia. C. Triskaidekaphobia. D. Glossophobia. List-II: 1. Water, 2. Snakes, 3. Number 13, 4. Public speaking.
questions.explanation: Hydro- = water; ophid- = snake (Greek 'ophis'); triskaideka- = 13 (Greek); glosso- = tongue (hence public speaking). Other niche ones to know — technophobia (technology), xenophobia (strangers/foreigners), photophobia (light — a symptom as well), thanatophobia (death), astraphobia (lightning / thunder).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

options.option_text: Has delusions of grandeur or power
Has an irrational fear of big objects

questions.explanation: Megalo- (Greek 'megas': great) + mania (madness, obsession). A megalomaniac has an exaggerated belief in their own importance, power or grandeur. Split personality / dissociative identity disorder is a different condition. Compulsive stealing = kleptomania. Fear of big objects = megalophobia (technically).
